description.narrative: The three-year Human rights and peace-building project to be implemented by HARD in Jur River County, South Sudan aims to create a stable peaceful environment where human rights for all are guaranteed. The project will empower women, youth and local leaders with knowledge of relevant laws that protect human rights especially rights of women and girls. In addition, the project will also promote local level building through increased knowledge in peace-building and facilitate establishment of community-level peace building structures. The target geographical area is characterised for rampant abuse of rights of women, girls and other vulnerable persons in the society. Assessments carried out in the County further indicate that there are widespread violent conflicts occasioned by; weak intuitions for conflict resolutions, lack of capacity in peace-building and ignorance. The project therefore intends to use community-based approaches to address the underlying factors impacting on human rights and conflicts. The target group are women leaders, youth leaders and local leaders who are influential and are opinion leaders within their communities. Most of these issues are rooted in culture that marginalises women and girls. The project will positively impact on women, girls and other vulnerable persons in the community like persons living with disability. There are a number of legal instruments both international and national that will be used to educate, train and sensitise local leaders on human rights and conflict resolution. The Transitional Constitution of South Sudan provides for respect of human rights of all citizens while, legislation such a; children’s Act 2008 outlaws practices such as child marriages. HARD being a national NGO that has been working in the area for many years have developed adequate expertise and rapport with the local communities that will be critical for the success of the project. HARD will benefit from technical support and guidance from CAFOD/Trocaire to successfully implement the project. There will be frequent visits to the project by CAFOD/Trocaire staff to provide technical support and advice to HARD staff.
